business_problem: Horizon needed to overhaul the storage, compute, and network foundation behind its autonomous-driving training workloads so it could support rapidly growing model volumes, higher concurrency, and the launch requirements of more than 100 new Journey 6 vehicle programs.
solution_summary: Baidu AI Cloud became Horizon's largest infrastructure supplier and rebuilt the core training stack for mass-production autonomous-driving models. On storage, Baidu optimized the bottom architecture to deliver EB-scale BOS object storage plus high-performance PFS parallel file storage for large data ingest and training throughput, including millisecond cross-cloud link support under very high query loads. For compute, Horizon deployed a very large CCE container cluster that can manage more than 100,000 concurrent pods and unify management of over 10,000 GPU cards, improving both operational efficiency and GPU pooling. Baidu and Horizon also automated GPU fault discovery and recovery so failures could be handled in minutes instead of interrupting long-running training. Network upgrades added dedicated links and bandwidth expansion to keep the training environment highly available. The overall design created a scalable AI-infrastructure base for Horizon's growing autonomous-driving portfolio while also adding data-compliance support for R&D and production workflows.

solution_components.name: BOS Object Storage
solution_components.role: Provides EB-scale object storage for autonomous-driving data and high-concurrency training access patterns.

solution_components.name: PFS Parallel File Storage
solution_components.role: Delivers the high-throughput shared file layer needed for large-scale model-training jobs.

solution_components.name: CCE Container Cluster
solution_components.role: Runs Horizon's large autonomous-driving training workloads with pooled GPU management and large-scale pod concurrency.

data_flow: Autonomous-driving data is stored in BOS and PFS, large training jobs run on the CCE container cluster with pooled GPU resources, automated monitoring handles GPU failures in minutes, and the upgraded network keeps data and model workloads moving reliably across the high-concurrency training environment.
business_outcome: Horizon gained a high-scale, stable AI foundation for mass-production autonomous-driving training, improving GPU utilization, shortening recovery from infrastructure failures, and supporting aggressive vehicle-program growth while extending into compliance operations.
metrics: 100+ Journey 6 vehicle models scheduled for mass production
GPU fault handling reduced to the minute level
architecture_clues: The storage layer uses both EB-scale object storage and high-performance parallel file storage for different autonomous-driving data patterns.
GPU failure detection and automated remediation are built into the cluster operations model.
Dedicated line reconstruction and bandwidth expansion were part of the final design, not just compute and storage upgrades.
